reconstruction.scope: Standing Temple of Vesta at Tivoli: roofless hollow dark-rubble cella with original simplified reticulate masonry patches with real southwest doorway and southeast window, blocked eastern relieving arch, ten surviving pale fluted Corinthian columns on the eastern/southern arc, partial curved entablature/annular coffered soffit and circular occupied podium with short southwest approach. Original simplified Tivoli-style floral capitals and horned skull/swag/rosette frieze; small restraint rods. Neighboring Temple of the Sibyl, restaurant furniture, cliff-retaining structures and landscaping remain separate host context. No restored absent columns, complete conical roof, copied inscription/sculpture or photo atlas.

reconstruction.heightBasis: Ordinary-picture/map estimates: cella radius4.6m/wall0.65m, column ring6.25m, podium radius7.25m, columns6.8m above level occupied floor, partial entablature to7.9m and irregular roofless cella top about7.1m. Door2.2x3.8m, southeast window1.1x1.9m with raised sill, blocked relieving arch3.5m wide. Ten columns, incomplete eastern/southern arc and original simplified relief/coffers; fine inventory, sculptural form, heights and absolute threshold levels remain estimates.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Retain pinned standard6m Mapzen cliff terrain, paths/water and all independent buildings. Level occupied podium floor is at least0.2m above its sampled7.25m envelope and0.6m above the coarse southwest approach; narrow perimeter footing bottoms follow retained ground and southwest steps descend to sampled approach. No surrounding acropolis slab, native ground/water cutout or terrain flattening. Coarse DEM blurs the cliff edge and cannot resolve archaeological paving/thresholds; exposed podium depths are visualization fit, not a measured ancient foundation section. Only matching cella shell is replaced; neighboring Sibyl/restaurant remain independent.
